## My Thinking

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over thirty years. My father farmed it before me. Everyone here does wheat and corn — winter wheat in October, summer corn right after the harvest in June. There's no point changing what works. My two children are working in the city, so it's mostly me and my wife now. I have 10 mu under contract.

The wheat season just ended. I'll replant the same rotation I've always done. I'll buy the Jimai variety from the county seed shop — my neighbor used it last year and got over 500 jin per mu. For the corn, I'll get Zhengdan 958, the hybrid everyone around here uses. It's reliable.

For fertilizer, I put down a base of diammonium phosphate and urea before planting, then topdress the wheat in spring at jointing. I know some people say to use less nitrogen, but I'd rather not risk a poor harvest. The extension station gave us a flyer last year about reducing fertilizer, but I've used this amount for years and it hasn't failed me.

Water is expensive to pump, but wheat needs it. I'll irrigate at overwinter, green-up, jointing, and heading — four times. The corn gets rain mostly in July and August here, so maybe just two irrigations unless it's a dry year.

I'll rotary till after the corn harvest to prep for wheat. After wheat harvest I plant corn almost immediately — no time for deep ploughing.
